a novel compound hetero-zygous mutation in STAMBP was identified in the first Chinese boy with MIC-CAM syndrome, which is characterized by developmental delay, microcephaly, intractable early-onset epilepsy, dyskinesia, capillary malformation and dysmorphic features, and the epilepsy in the patient is refractory.
the present study reported a novel compound heterogenous mutation of the STAMPB gene in a patient with MIC-CAP, and the patient presented with early-onset epilepsy and developmental delay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel STAM-BP mutation in a patient with MIC-CAP, which may be a potential cause of epilepsy and developmental delay.
the identification of a new compound heterozygote mutation in the STAMB gene, which may provide a novel target for future genetic testing and treatment.
a case of MIC-CAP syndrome in a Chinese boy caused by a novel mutation in the STAMPB gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIC-CAP syndrome is characterized by early-onset epilepsy and severe neurodevelopmental delay, and the STAMBP mutation is associated with this syndrome.
STAMBP gene mutations may lead to early-onset refractory epilepsy in patients with MIC-CAP, and that this may be the first reported Chinese patient with MIC-CAP caused by a STAMBP mutation.

STAMBP mutations cause MIC-CAP syndrome, which is characterized by intractable early-onset epilepsy, microcephaly, capillary malformation, dyskinesia and developmental delay, and that STAMBP gene mutation screening is necessary for the diagnosis of MIC-CAP syndrome in cases with early-onset epilepsy and dyskinesia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STAMBP gene mutation is the main cause of MIC-CAP syndrome.
STAMBP mutations are a cause of epilepsy and developmental delay in patients with MIC-CAP, and that STAMBP gene sequencing is recommended for patients with epilepsy and developmental delay.
the STAMBP mutation was associated with a poor outcome, and the clinical features of the present patient with MIC-CAP were consistent with previously reported patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STAMBP gene testing should be considered in the evaluation of children with early-onset intractable epilepsy, developmental delay and dysmorphic features.
STAMBP gene testing should be considered in patients with epilepsy and microcephalic features.
STAMBP mutations should be considered in the differential diagnosis of early-onset epilepsy and/or microcephaly, especially in cases with a family history of epilepsy.
